program_name: Management Engineering (English-taught curriculum) — Italian official name: Corso di laurea magistrale in Ingegneria Gestionale, curriculum "Management Engineering". The LM-31 degree hosts two curricula; this record covers ONLY the curriculum whose teaching is entirely in English, listed by UNIUD as "Master's degree in Management Engineering" among the "Degrees taught entirely in English".
teaching_language: English — 100% of the teaching in this curriculum is delivered in English. UNIUD lists "Master's degree in Management Engineering" in its official list of "Master's degree courses taught entirely in English". The parent LM-31 degree also contains a second, separate curriculum ("Ingegneria Gestionale") that is taught mainly in Italian with only some English modules — that Italian-majority track is NOT covered here and requires Italian B2. In the official non-EU vacant-places table the row "MANAGEMENT ENGINEERING curriculum taught in English" shows a dash ("-") under "Required Italian proficiency", i.e. no Italian language certificate is required for the English track.
campus: Udine (Department of Engineering and Architecture / Dipartimento Politecnico di Ingegneria e Architettura – DPIA, Via delle Scienze 206, Udine). The manifesto lists "Ingegneria Gestionale *** (LM-31 Ingegneria gestionale) – sede di Udine". No branch campus (unlike some other Italian programmes hosted elsewhere).
degree_class: LM-31 (Ingegneria gestionale / Management engineering). Single class, not an interclass. Note for disambiguation: the neighbouring English-taught UNIUD master "Industrial Engineering for Sustainable Manufacturing" IS an interclass LM-31/LM-33 — this Management Engineering degree is not.
admission_type: Hybrid: the Italian-system degree itself is open access ("accesso libero" — no numero programmato, no national/local quota, no admission test in the Italian sense), BUT applicants holding a foreign qualification must go through a compulsory pre-evaluation selection call on the Elix-Forms platform, and the English-taught international track is capped at 20 slots per academic year filled on a rolling CV-evaluation basis. So in practice, for the international audience it behaves as a 'selection call' with a capped, first-come/rolling intake rather than truly free access.
access_type_detail: Degree-level: "accesso libero" (open access) — the LM-31 Ingegneria Gestionale degree is not listed among UNIUD's nationally regulated or locally regulated ("numero programmato") courses in the 2026/2027 additional notices; those lists cover only Medicine, Architecture, Healthcare Professions, Primary Teacher Education, Sport Sciences, Biotechnology, Building and Territory Technology and Public Relations. Track-level: the English-taught international master track has 20 slots per academic year, allocated by CV evaluation and CLOSED once the maximum number of slots is reached — i.e. a rolling cap, not a ranked graduatoria published at a fixed date. Separately, Attachment 1 to the 2026/2027 Additional Notice assigns 20 places reserved for prospective students resident in non-EU countries to the row "MANAGEMENT ENGINEERING curriculum taught in English" (a distinct row from the plain "MANAGEMENT ENGINEERING" master, which also has 20 non-EU places but requires Italian B2). [uncertain] It is not stated on any UNIUD page whether the '20 slots per academic year' on the programme page and the '20 non-EU reserved places' in Attachment 1 are the same 20 places or two separate allocations, nor whether EU-resident international applicants draw from the same 20-slot pool.
academic_requirements: For applicants with a foreign qualification (the English track's target audience), UNIUD states three cumulative requirements: (1) "A relevant Bachelor's degree (Industrial Engineering or IT Engineering), obtained within the last five years" — the Additional Notice's requirements table words this as "Bachelor degree in Industrial or Information Engineering obtained in the last five years"; (2) "Final grade: >= 90/110 (Italian system) or >= 3/4 of the maximum (foreign equivalent)" — the Additional Notice table states "The final grade of the bachelor degree must be not less than 3/4 of the maximum possible"; (3) "At least B1 CEFR level of English". The foreign bachelor must additionally be an official first-cycle degree issued by an accredited institution in its own education system and must give access to equivalent second-cycle courses there; its eligibility is verified via a CIMEA Statement or a Declaration of Value (ARDI holders from Lisbon Convention signatory countries must still request the CIMEA Verification Statement). Underlying Italian-system curricular requirements for all LM Engineering courses at UNIUD (relevant if an applicant is assessed against the ordinary route): at least 45 CFU in the SSDs of the basic training activities and at least 80 further CFU in the characterising SSDs; for Ingegneria Gestionale the characterising list is ING-IND/13, ING-IND/16, ING-IND/17, ING-IND/31, ING-IND/32, ING-IND/34, ING-IND/35, ING-INF/01-07 (alternative route: ING-IND/01-28, ING-IND/31-35, ING-INF/04, ING-INF/06-07, ICAR/08, FIS/04). Personal preparation and aptitude are verified by the course teaching committee through evaluation of the previous academic career and a possible test or interview; candidates with a graduation mark of not less than 90/110 are exempt from that test/interview.
entry_exam_or_test: No written entrance examination and no TOLC. TOLC-I at UNIUD applies only to the BACHELOR engineering courses (including the bachelor in Ingegneria Gestionale), not to this master. Selection for the English track is by CV evaluation carried out by the Academic/Admissions Committee on the Elix-Forms pre-evaluation application. An ONLINE INTERVIEW may be used in two situations: (a) where the candidate has no B2 (here B1) English certificate, "the competent Academic Committee may assess English language skills through an online interview"; (b) for Italian-system candidates whose bachelor final mark is below 90/110, the teaching committee may set a test or colloquium to verify personal preparation. [uncertain] For master's applicants the 2026/2027 notices describe the interview as discretionary (only the outcome is guaranteed within 30 working days), whereas for the English-taught BACHELOR (MBA) the non-EU notice says the Committee "will schedule an online selection interview"; UNIUD does not explicitly state whether an interview is systematically scheduled for every Management Engineering applicant.
entry_test_name_and_deadline: No named entry test. The operative deadline is the Elix-Forms pre-evaluation application deadline: applications for master's degree courses taught in Italian or English must be submitted between 01/02/2026 and 10/09/2026 for applicants RESIDENT IN EU COUNTRIES, and between 01/02/2026 and 31/05/2026 for applicants RESIDENT IN NON-EU COUNTRIES. Because the English track's 20 slots are filled on a rolling basis and closed once full, applying early inside the window matters more than the nominal end date. OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning requirements) do NOT apply to this master — the 2026/27 Engineering manifesto assigns OFA only to the listed bachelor courses (students who have not taken TOLC-I by 15 January 2027 or who score below 6/20 in the Mathematics sections). For the master, the equivalent 'gap' mechanism is the possible preparation interview, plus the option of acquiring missing CFU as single courses (corsi singoli) before enrolment. There is no post-enrolment test to sit.
reserved_places_non_eu: 20 places reserved for prospective students resident in non-EU countries, per Attachment 1 to the 2026/2027 Additional Notice to the study Prospectus, row: DPIA / M / "MANAGEMENT ENGINEERING curriculum taught in English" — 20 places, Required Italian proficiency: "-" (none), Required English proficiency: B1. This row is separate from DPIA / M / "MANAGEMENT ENGINEERING" (the Italian-majority track), which also lists 20 non-EU places but with Italian B2 required. [uncertain] Whether these 20 non-EU reserved places are carved out of, or additional to, the 20 total international slots announced on the programme page is not clarified in any official UNIUD document.
admin_seat_university: University of Udine (UNIUD) is the sole administering university — this is NOT an inter-university (interateneo) or joint programme, so admission, pre-evaluation, enrolment (immatricolazione via Esse3), tuition and student records are all handled by UNIUD's Segreteria Studenti / Department of Engineering and Architecture (DPIA). Double-degree options exist but do not change the administrative seat: per the 2026/27 Engineering manifesto footnote ***, the double degree agreements (Master Degree in International Industrial Management MSc with FH Joanneum University of Applied Sciences, Graz; and MSc with Alpen-Adria Universitaet Klagenfurt, Austria) are attached to the "Ingegneria Gestionale" curriculum of the degree. [uncertain] The manifesto footnote ties the Austrian double degrees to the Italian-named "Ingegneria Gestionale" curriculum; UNIUD does not state whether students on the English-taught "Management Engineering" curriculum can access the same double-degree tracks.
course_status_flag: Active and fully operational — NOT 'ad esaurimento'. The 2026/27 Engineering manifesto lists "Ingegneria Gestionale *** (LM-31 Ingegneria gestionale) – sede di Udine, Anni di corso attivati: tutti" (all years of the course activated), and the English curriculum appears in the 2026/2027 international admission documents and in the current official list of degrees taught entirely in English. The English curriculum was introduced in academic year 2023-24 ("nell'anno accademico 2023-24 l'offerta della LM in ingegneria gestionale è stata arricchita con un nuovo curriculum i cui insegnamenti sono interamente in lingua inglese"), so it is a recent addition rather than a course being phased out.
language_requirements: ENGLISH: at least B1 CEFR (programme-specific exception; see english_level_exception). The certificate must clearly indicate the achieved level and must have been obtained within the last 5 years. Recognised certifying bodies listed by UNIUD: Cambridge English Language Assessment; Trinity College London; IELTS; TOEFL; Pearson Edexcel — Test of English Academic (PTE Academic); Pearson General English; Oxford Test of English; LanguageCert International ESOL; Gatehouse Awards Classic; British Council – Aptis ESOL General; British Council – Aptis ESOL Advanced. EXEMPTIONS: applicants who have completed a school programme taught in English (IB diplomas, multilingual schools, etc.) or who are native English speakers (per the UK gov.uk English-language exemptions list referenced by UNIUD) are exempt from providing a certificate. FLEXIBILITY: "It is possible to submit the pre-evaluation application even without the required language certification, provided that the candidate is awaiting the English language test or the issuance of the certification" — but obtaining it remains necessary to complete enrolment. If no certificate at the required level is held, "the competent Academic Committee may assess English language skills through an online interview". ITALIAN: none required for this English-taught curriculum — Attachment 1 shows "-" in the 'Required Italian proficiency' column for the row "MANAGEMENT ENGINEERING curriculum taught in English". (By contrast the Italian-majority Management Engineering track requires Italian B2 via a CLIQ-system certificate: CELI / CILS / CERTIT / PLIDA.)
english_level_exception: YES — this is UNIUD's only documented programme-specific English exception. Both the EU and non-EU 2026/2027 Additional Notices state verbatim: "For the Master's degree course in Management Engineering, the required level of English language proficiency is B1." The standalone Language Requirements sheet repeats it: "To access to degree courses taught entirely in English, a B2-level English proficiency or an equivalent certification is required. For the Master's degree course in Management Engineering, the required English proficiency level is B1 or equivalent." All other UNIUD degrees taught entirely in English (Economics; International Marketing, Management and Organization; Artificial Intelligence & Cybersecurity; Industrial Engineering for Sustainable Manufacturing; the bachelor in Management & Business Analytics) require B2. Note also the rule that "For degree courses taught partially in English, the required level of proficiency in both Italian and English remains B2 or equivalent" — so an applicant who ends up on the Italian-majority curriculum would face B2 in both languages, not B1.
english_cert_validity_years: 5 years. UNIUD's general rule applies unchanged to this programme: "Only certificates obtained within the last 5 years will be considered valid. Certificates must clearly indicate the achieved level." No programme-specific derogation from the 5-year rule exists; the Management Engineering exception concerns the LEVEL (B1 instead of B2), not the validity period.
teaching_language_partial_flag: "English curriculum track exists; the other track is mainly Italian" — the LM-31 Ingegneria Gestionale degree runs two parallel curricula: (1) "Management Engineering" — entirely in English (the subject of this record); (2) "Ingegneria Gestionale" — mainly in Italian with some English modules, articulated into five thematic paths (Advanced Manufacturing, Industrial Management, Environmental Sustainability, Digital Business and Analytics, Information & Communication Technology). Choosing the English curriculum gives a fully English study path with no Italian certificate requirement; choosing the Italian curriculum requires Italian B2 (and, if it is treated as partially English, B2 in both languages). Applicants must be careful: the degree's generic Italian pages describe the delivery language as Italian, and the non-EU vacant-places table lists the two tracks as separate rows with different language requirements.
application_deadline_eu: 01/02/2026 – 10/09/2026 (Elix-Forms pre-evaluation window for applicants RESIDENT IN EU COUNTRIES holding a foreign qualification). Official wording: "Applications for admission to master's degree courses taught in Italian and in English must be submitted on the Elix-Forms platform between 01/02/2026 and 10/09/2026." WARNING: this nominal end date can be overtaken by the 20-slot cap, which closes the international track once filled; and enrolment itself must be completed by 5 October 2026 at 12:00, leaving very little margin for a 10 September application.
application_deadline_non_eu: 01/02/2026 – 31/05/2026 (Elix-Forms pre-evaluation window for applicants RESIDENT IN NON-EU COUNTRIES). Official wording: "Applications for admission to Master's degree courses taught in Italian or English must be submitted through the Elix-Forms platform between 01/02/2026 and 31/05/2026." This is more than three months earlier than the EU window because the non-EU path must leave time for the letter of eligibility, Universitaly pre-enrolment by 30 June 2026 and study-visa issuance.
universitaly_deadline: 30 June 2026 — a SEPARATE deadline from the UNIUD pre-evaluation deadline and applicable only to applicants needing a study visa. Official wording: prospective students "MUST create their digital profile on the UNIVERSITALY portal ... and submit the digital PRE-ENROLMENT application for a degree course at the University of Udine for the academic year 2026/2027 by the 30th of June 2026 at the latest. Pre-enrolment applications submitted after the 30th of June 2026 will not be considered." Documents to attach on Universitaly: valid passport; passport-sized photograph; first-cycle university degree (or final/provisional single-cycle master's degree) for second-cycle applicants; and, for English-taught courses, the English language proficiency certificate. Binding consequences: a visa applicant may enrol only in the degree course chosen on Universitaly, and changing degree course after arrival — or transferring to another Italian university during the first year — is not permitted. Note the practical sequencing trap: the non-EU pre-evaluation closes 31/05/2026 and Universitaly closes 30/06/2026, so the UNIUD letter of eligibility must arrive within that one-month gap (the 30-working-day decision clock makes this tight for late-May applications).
decision_timeline_days: 30 working days. The Academic Committee "will communicate the outcome of the assessment to the applicant via email within 30 working days from the date of submission" (EU notice) / "within 30 working days from the date of submission" the outcome is communicated after the CV evaluation and any online interview (non-EU notice). Successful applicants then receive by email the letter of eligibility for enrolment.
enrolment_window: 9 July 2026 – 5 October 2026, 12:00 noon, for all master's degree courses: "Le domande d'immatricolazione ai corsi di laurea magistrale si presentano dal 9 luglio 2026 al 5 ottobre 2026, con proroga che può essere concessa dal Rettore, per giustificati motivi, fino al 31 marzo 2027, dietro presentazione di un'istanza di immatricolazione in ritardo in marca da bollo da € 16,00." No late-application petition is needed for students who obtain their bachelor's degree after 5 October 2026. Enrolment is completed online on the Esse3 platform and is only perfected once the first tuition instalment is paid within the peremptory deadline — non-payment means exclusion from the enrolment procedure; postal applications are not accepted. CHRONOLOGICAL / CAPACITY WARNING specific to this programme: the international track has 20 slots and "the selection ... will be closed once the maximum number of available slots is reached", so places go on a rolling first-evaluated basis rather than by a published ranking. Additionally, "Courses start at the end of September, and students must already be in Udine by then", and non-EU students are explicitly warned to plan visa, travel and accommodation accordingly.
required_documents: For the Elix-Forms pre-evaluation application to a second-cycle (master's) degree course, UNIUD requires scanned copies of: (a) foreign final or provisional university qualification (bachelor); (b) list of completed exams / transcript of records / diploma supplement of the foreign bachelor; (c) descriptions of single subjects / syllabus of the foreign bachelor; (d) valid passport; (e) updated curriculum vitae; (f) CIMEA Statements or Declaration of Value of the foreign bachelor; (g) required language certification. Items (f) and (g) are footnoted: "It may also be submitted after the online pre-evaluation procedure, but it is required for the final enrolment procedure at the University of Udine." A non-refundable €20.00 application fee must be paid (via PagoPA, or by bank transfer in specific cases) — "only complete applications will be evaluated, meaning the applications for which the required fee has been duly paid." Because selection for this programme is CV-based, the curriculum vitae is the decisive document. For non-EU visa applicants, a further Universitaly document set is required by 30 June 2026: valid passport; passport-sized photograph; first-cycle university degree; English proficiency certificate (B2 or equivalent per the generic Universitaly wording — B1 for this programme per the programme-specific rule). At final enrolment on Esse3, graduates from other universities must also self-certify the degree obtained and the exams passed, with credits, marks and scientific-disciplinary sectors. [uncertain] A motivation letter is explicitly listed among required documents only for the English-taught BACHELOR (Management & Business Analytics) application; the master's document list (a)–(g) does not name a motivation letter, though the Application Presentation Guide may request one in practice.

uncertainty_notes: (1) DOUBLE-COUNTING OF THE NUMBER 20: the programme page's "20 slots per academic year" for the international master programme and Attachment 1's "20 places reserved to future students resident in non E.U. Countries" for the row "MANAGEMENT ENGINEERING curriculum taught in English" are both 20, but no UNIUD document says whether they are the same allocation or two distinct pools (i.e. whether EU-resident international applicants compete for the same 20 slots or have a separate allowance). Treat the safe planning assumption as: at most 20 international students per year in total on the English curriculum. (2) INTERVIEW: for master's applicants the notices frame the online interview as discretionary (used mainly to assess English where no certificate is held, or to verify personal preparation where the bachelor mark is below 90/110); for the English-taught bachelor (Management & Business Analytics) the non-EU notice states an interview WILL be scheduled. It is not clear whether Management Engineering applicants are systematically interviewed. (3) MOTIVATION LETTER: named as required for the English-taught bachelor application but absent from the master's document list (a)–(g); the Application Presentation Guide (a 3.1 MB PDF that could not be parsed as text) may add requirements not reflected here. (4) TWO-TRACK CONFUSION RISK: the generic Italian pages of the LM-31 degree describe the delivery language as Italian and quote only the ordinary Italian access rules (45+80 CFU, colloquium, exemption at 90/110); only the international notices and the programme's English page describe the English curriculum's specific selection (CV, 20 slots, B1, degree within 5 years). Applicants who apply through the ordinary Italian route may be enrolled into the Italian-majority curriculum, which requires Italian B2 and, if treated as partially English, B2 in both languages. (5) DOUBLE DEGREES: the manifesto footnote attaches the FH Joanneum Graz and Alpen-Adria Klagenfurt double degrees explicitly to the "Ingegneria Gestionale" curriculum; availability of these to English-curriculum students is not documented. (6) NOT AN INTERATENEO PROGRAMME: unlike some UNIUD offerings (e.g. the Udine–Trieste inter-university healthcare courses), this degree has no partner administering university — UNIUD is the sole seat for admission, enrolment and fees. Do not confuse it with the separate UNIUD English-taught master "Industrial Engineering for Sustainable Manufacturing", which is an interclass LM-31/LM-33 and requires B2 English.
